finding.problem: The wording-only bypass rests on a flag the approver sets on the approve_commit call itself (params.wording_only). Nothing checks that the commit's change is actually wording only, such as a diff classification or the change check. Any approver can skip the change check on any commit by passing true. This removes the guarantee that a change is checked before approval. The record_approval precondition and the invariant then accept the same self-asserted value (target.wording_only), so they no longer guard anything.

findings.label: seeded
findings.why: It identifies that the edit lets a commit be approved without a passing change check via a self-asserted flag, which conflicts with the rule that approval requires a passing check.

finding.problem: The invariant approved-commits-passed-their-checks is now false by its own name. Approved commits may never have been checked, and the check is satisfied by an unverified flag. The reason on the check_commit precondition not-approved still says 'An approved commit passed its check', which no longer holds. The glossary says the change check is what a commit runs 'before approval', and the Purpose announcement says 'Every change shows what it breaks before anything is deployed'. Both now overstate what happens.

findings.label: seeded
findings.why: It notes the invariant approved-commits-passed-their-checks is now violated by allowing unchecked approvals, which is the same conflict with the key's rule.

finding.problem: approve_commit sets target.wording_only = params.wording_only whenever it runs. A call that omits the optional param can overwrite or clear a wording_only value already on the commit. The precondition reads params.wording_only, while the later record_approval precondition and the invariant read target.wording_only. The two sources can disagree, for example if the flag is set on the target some other way, and the approver's claim is never reconciled with the stored value.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: The precondition reads params.wording_only while later checks read target.wording_only, and the effect overwrites the stored value, a real inconsistency distinct from the seeded conflict.

finding.problem: Commit.wording_only has no check_commit or record_check path, and the existing Element.wording_only is set at propose time. The new Commit flag has the same name but a different origin and trust level. No example covers the new wording-only approval path, and the existing example 'approve-only-after-a-passing-check' no longer states the whole rule, since a wording-only approval now bypasses that check. The kernel's own `approve_commit` call may also still refuse an unchecked commit, so the declared bypass may not work or may fail only at the kernel.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: The existing example approve-only-after-a-passing-check no longer states the whole rule and the new flag has no covered path, which is a real but secondary problem.

edit.why: It adds a wording_only path that lets approve_commit proceed without a passing check and updates the precondition, record_approval check, and invariant accordingly.
